chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Sayf ibn Ameyra, who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Jibraeel (peace be upon him) came to Yusuf (peace be upon him) while he was in prison, and he said to him: O Yusuf! Say at the end of every prayer.'
O Allah! Make for me a relief and an exit, and provide for me from where I expect and from where I do not expect.
ai.seo_question: What supplication did Jibraeel teach Prophet Yusuf to recite after prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual sustenance by linking the supplication of Prophet Yusuf (peace be upon him) in prison to the post-prayer du'a, emphasizing divine provision from both expected and unexpected sources. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that specific du'as serve as spiritual anchors during trials, mirroring Yusuf’s patience and eventual elevation. The emphasis on 'rizq' (sustenance) connects physical relief with spiritual trust in Allah’s timing.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Sayf Bin Ameyra who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘Jibraeelas came over to Yusufas while heas was in the prison, and heas said to himas: ‘O Yusufas! Say at the end of every Salāt:

‘O Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>! Make a relief for me<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> and an exit, and Grace me<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> from where I<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> do expect and from where I<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> do not expect (it to be from)’’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from Sayf ibn ‘Amirah who has said the following: “I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘Jibril (Gabriel) came to Joseph in prison and said to him, “Joseph, after every prayer say, ‘
O Lord, grant me relief, a way out (of difficulties), and sustenance from the sources I expect and from those I do not expect.’”
